subject: Subprocessor onboarding + on-call handover / retention exception request
messages:
From: Patricia Li <patricia.li@aerostream.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: AeroStream Security <security@aerostream.com>, AeroStream Procurement <procurement@aerostream.com>
Date: Mon, 13 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Intro: CloudOps onboarding (logging + on-call) — DPA/evidence ask

Hi Grace,

Following up from our vendor intake call: AeroStream is planning to engage CloudOps Inc. as a subprocessor to manage cluster logging and a small on-call rotation for incident escalation. CloudOps will not have persistent access to customer payloads — they ingest trimmed logs for alerting and retain for a short window for troubleshooting.

What we need from Redwood to progress:
- Confirmation this subprocessor is acceptable under the MSA Order Form redline (we flagged Section 5.2 / Subprocessors).
- A DPA addendum or template you require executed, plus the minimal evidence packet (SOC2 or iso attestation) you need for MLB review.
- An exception/acknowledgement on retention: CloudOps requests a 30-day log retention window vs. our standard 90 days for this specific service. If that requires an Order Form carve-out, please advise expected path and timing.
- On-call handover: points of contact and escalation SLA mapping so CloudOps' team can be added to our rotation for P1 alerts (read-only ops access only).

I've attached CloudOps' attestation and a summary of their controls (aerostream_subproc_attestation.pdf). Happy to hop on a quick sync if helpful — procurement and security are copied.

Thanks,
Patricia
Head of Vendor Ops
AeroStream

--
Attachments: aerostream_subproc_attestation.pdf (PDF, 345 KB)
From: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.inference.com>
To: Patricia Li <patricia.li@aerostream.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.inference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Sep 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Intro: CloudOps onboarding (logging + on-call) — DPA/evidence ask

Patricia — thanks for the note and the attachment. Quick answers below and a follow-up ask for Kimberly/legal.

High level: we are open to CloudOps onboarding for trimmed logging and on-call as long as the flow-down and access controls meet Section 4/5 of our MSA and the Order Form explicitly captures the retention carve-out.

Action items for Redwood legal/procurement (cc'd):
- Kimberly: please confirm whether the 30-day retention can be handled as an Order Form clause vs a DPA amendment. If Order Form is sufficient, we'll produce a redline draft.
- Marissa: can you confirm what evidence package we require to close the security review (SOC2 Type II, encryption-in-transit proof, limited admin access attestation). If CloudOps' attestation is insufficient we'll need the additional artifacts.
- Patricia: please have CloudOps confirm (in writing) they will only hold trimmed logs, that they will not persist raw customer payloads, and provide a primary contact for on-call onboarding.

I attached a quick set of suggested Order Form redlines (orderform_redlines_Grace_v2.pdf) — Kimberly/Marissa please use as starting point.

If all looks plausible, I'll schedule a 30-minute alignment on Thursday to close the path to signature.

Best,
Grace
Director, Customer Success
Redwood Inference

--
Attachments: orderform_redlines_Grace_v2.pdf (PDF, 42 KB)
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly@redwood.inference.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace@redwood.inference.com>, Patricia Li <patricia.li@aerostream.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.inference.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor@redwood.inference.com>
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2026 08:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Intro: CloudOps onboarding (logging + on-call) — legal view + next steps

Grace / Patricia — I reviewed the attestation and Grace's suggested Order Form redlines. Summary and next steps:

Summary:
- MSA references: Section 5 (Subprocessors) requires flow-down of security and data handling obligations. For a third party that stores logs even short-term, we require either: (A) order form-level carve-out + specific DPA language that limits retention and access, or (B) execution of the standard DPA with an explicit Subprocessor Schedule.
- Retention: 30 days is acceptable in principle as a negotiated deviation. It must be explicit in the Order Form and mirrored in the Subprocessor Schedule of the DPA.
- Evidence: CloudOps' attestation is a start. We also need either a recent SOC2 Type II report or a completed security questionnaire and a screenshot of their logging pipeline showing redaction/trimming.
- On-call: we will only permit read-only alerting access; any escalations that require tenant-level investigation must be performed by Redwood engineers or AeroStream's on-call.

Requested changes (redlines attached as DPA_template_subproc_track.docx and inline notes in Grace's PDF):
1) Add Subprocessor Schedule reference in the Order Form (clause: Subprocessor Authorization & Retention).
2) Add an explicit retention field: "Log retention for CloudOps: 30 days (trimmed logs); no raw payload retention."
3) Require attestations + SOC2 or equivalent evidence within 7 business days of onboarding.
4) Add a one-way indemnity carve-out for breaches caused by CloudOps' failure to safeguard trimmed logs (language provided).

Patricia — can you confirm CloudOps can provide SOC2 Type II or complete our questionnaire within 7 business days and that they accept a DPA Subprocessor Schedule? If not, we will need a stronger compensating control documented. Also please provide the primary on-call contact (name + phone + emails) so we can scope the limited access required for PagerDuty integration.

I'll circulate a redline DPA and Order Form in the next 24 hours. Connor — can you estimate how much dev work is required to set read-only alerting integration (PagerDuty webhook + masked log stream)? It's likely a small hook but want to set expectations for ops timelines.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Sr. Counsel, Contracts
Redwood Inference

--

Kimberly / Grace — thanks for the speedy review. Quick replies:
- CloudOps confirms they can execute the Subprocessor Schedule in the DPA and accept a 30-day retention clause for trimmed logs.
- They do not have a public SOC2 Type II report yet; they can complete our standard security questionnaire (filled) and provide an on-demand SOC2 readiness report and system architecture screenshots within 5 business days.
- Primary on-call: Marco Reyes <marco.reyes@cloudops.io>, +1 415-555-0122. He can be added to a read-only PagerDuty rotation for P1 alerts.

I have attached their returned questionnaire and the attestation (aerostream_subproc_attestation.pdf) for your review and uploaded the evidence bundle to the Drive link above. Procurement is prepared to accept the DPA Subprocessor Schedule if legal signs off — they asked whether Redwood can issue a DocuSign envelope once final.

DocuSign path is fine — we typically sign AeroStream-side after Redwood counters.

Best,
Patricia
